fib: ______ is the regulatory institution of the insurance sub-sector in Nigeria.
National Insurance commission
The National Insurance commission is the regulatory institution of the insurance sub-sector in Nigeria.
______ is a tripartite agreement between the customer on the first part, the third party liable to pay on the second part and the bank on the third part.
Domiciliation of Payment
Domiciliation of Payment is a tripartite agreement between the customer on the first part, the third party liable to pay on the second part and the bank on the third part.
______ is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
NAICOM
NAICOM is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
______ is a conveyance of interest in a property as security for the payment of a debt or for the discharge of some other obligation.
mortgage
A mortgage is a conveyance of interest in a property as security for the payment of a debt or for the discharge of some other obligation.
______ is an undertaking by a person to pay the debt of another in case that other person fails to pay.
guarantee
A guarantee is an undertaking by a person to pay the debt of another in case that other person fails to pay.
______ is a charge created by a company over specified assets.
fixed charge
A fixed charge is a charge created by a company over specified assets.
______ is a banking practice that regulates dealings with a customer multiple accounts with a particular bank especially when those accounts are in debt.
Appropriation of payment
Appropriation of payment is a banking practice that regulates dealings with a customer multiple accounts with a particular bank especially when those accounts are in debt.
______ is a right that is available to the bank.
Combination of accounts
Combination of accounts is a right that is available to the bank.
______ is one of the recognized ways in which a customer can borrow money from the bank.
Overdraft
Overdraft is one of the recognized ways in which a customer can borrow money from the bank.
